title: Pikachu plush returns from a real space trip
summary:
A special Pikachu plush toy spent 67 days aboard the International Space Station. The European Space Agency, or ESA, announced the trip on September 19, 2026.

The toy travelled to the station on April 11 in a Cygnus cargo spacecraft. Cargo means supplies or other things being carried. It returned to Earth on June 17 aboard a SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft.

While in orbit, Pikachu made about 1,040 trips around Earth. An orbit is the path an object follows around a planet or another body in space.

The journey is part of a project celebrating World Space Week 2026, which runs from October 4 to 10. An exhibition brings Pokémon characters together with real information about European space missions and life on the station.

The exhibition began in Paris in late September. It will travel to museums and other places across Europe through April 2027.

Participating European science and space museums will also offer special Pokémon GO activities. ESA hopes the project will encourage children and teenagers to become curious about space and science.
why_it_matters: The project connects a familiar Pokémon character with information about real space missions. ESA hopes this will encourage children and teenagers to explore space and science.
